specification.problem: Dynamic percolation quantum walk on a 4-site cycle: each step draws a random edge-presence mask, giving a random unitary channel whose long-time limit is set by the peripheral spectrum. The circuit simulates one fixed mask sequence (a single trajectory); averaging over sequences is classical.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Single trajectory of a coined Hadamard walk on a 4-cycle, T fixed classical masks compiled into gates, with explicit initial-state preparation |x=0>|c=+> and an explicit permutation convention for the shift. The ensemble channel and its asymptotic attractor are background, computed classically. The 2D Grover-coin lattice, the paper's own asymptotic construction and its numerical example are out of scope.

symbols.meaning: edge mask; \omega_e=1 means edge e joining sites e and e+1 mod 4 is open
probability an edge is open, independent per edge and step
permutation of basis labels (x,c) realized by S_\omega

equations.label: Step unitary for fixed mask
equations.description: Coin first, then shift with reflection (coin flip, no move) at closed edges. Positions mod 4. S_\omega is a basis permutation: |x,R> goes to |x+1,R> if edge x is open, else to |x,L>; |x,L> goes to |x-1,L> if edge x-1 is open, else to |x,R>. Closed edge x: |x,R>->|x,L> and |x+1,L>->|x+1,R>. These are images distinct from the others, so S is a bijection.
equations.justification: Concrete percolation shift for the minimal instance; the abstract does not give the shift rule.
assumptions: Edge e joins sites e and e+1 mod 4

equations.label: Permutation convention
equations.description: The circuit must map basis state s to pi(s) (forward direction, not its inverse). Index s=x+4c... with little-endian qubits: x0,x1 are qubits 0,1 and coin is qubit 2, so index = x+4c. Verify the compiled circuit by comparing its Operator with the dense matrix of eq_1 for several masks, including the full product in eq_3.
equations.justification: Addresses the review: fixes direction and encoding so the permutation decomposition can be checked.

equations.label: Trajectory state
equations.description: Circuit output for a fixed mask sequence. The circuit must begin with an explicit H on the coin qubit (qubit 2) before the step loop, since the circuit starts in |0,0>.
equations.justification: Defines the implementable unitary for one realization, including the initial-state preparation missing from the earlier build.
assumptions: Masks are classical parameters compiled into gates

equations.label: Random unitary channel
equations.description: Mask-averaged one-step dynamics; state after T steps is Phi^T(rho_0).
equations.abstract_quote: the connections appear and disappear randomly in each step during the time evolution
equations.justification: Random edge presence at each step gives a random unitary map; the product form of P assumes independent identical edges.

equations.label: Peripheral/attractor space
equations.latex: \Phi^T(\rho)\to\Phi_\infty(\rho),\quad \text{peripheral eigenoperators }X:\ U_\omega X U_\omega^\dagger=\lambda X\ \forall\omega\text{ with }P(\omega)>0,\ |\lambda|=1
equations.description: Standard random-unitary-map asymptotics: the long-time limit lives on the span of peripheral eigenoperators; the rest decays. Recalled background, not the paper's formulas.
equations.justification: Known result for finite-dimensional unital channels with unitary Kraus operators.

equations.label: Position distribution
equations.description: Per-trajectory distribution, averaged classically over N sampled sequences to approximate the channel (Monte Carlo, approximate).
equations.justification: Output decoding for the trajectory circuit.
assumptions: Monte Carlo averaging over N sampled sequences

specification.initial_state: |x=0>|c=0> from the circuit start, then an explicit Hadamard on the coin qubit gives |x=0>|c=+>.

steps.description: Prepare the initial state: apply H on coin qubit 2 before any step.

For t=1..T apply the Hadamard coin on qubit 2, then the shift S_omega_t as the basis permutation pi_omega_t (forward direction, index=x+4c), compiled from the classical mask with multi-controlled X/swap gates or a permutation unitary.
Validate: compare the circuit Operator against the dense product of eq_1 matrices applied after the initial H for several masks; fix permutation order or direction if they differ.
Classically sample mask sequences with P(omega), simulate each, compute position distributions and average. Peripheral analysis is done classically on the 64x64 superoperator.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis position measurement on the final state, or exact probabilities from the statevector, per trajectory.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average position distributions over sampled sequences. Optionally diagonalize Phi (64x64 superoperator) for the peripheral eigenspace.
assumptions: The 4-cycle, Hadamard coin and reflecting closed-edge rule are choices of this reconstruction
The circuit is a single trajectory with classical masks, not the open-system channel
No black-box query complexity is claimed
